title: Crowded and empty: where the world's people live
examples: Why do so many people live by rivers?

groups.label: Crowded places
groups.ask: Why do so many people live in river valleys?

groups.label: Almost empty

explain.say: If the world’s 8 billion people were spread evenly over all the land, there would be about 55 people on every square kilometre. But people are not spread evenly at all! Look at the board. We will sort places into crowded and almost empty, and find the reasons.

explain.say: Population density means how many people live on each square kilometre. Look at the crowded places: the Ganges plain in India, the Nile valley in Egypt and the island of Java in Indonesia. What do they share? Flat land, rich soil, plenty of water and warmth for farming. Can you spot the river link?

groups.label: Almost empty
groups.ask: Why do so few people live in deserts and mountains?

explain.say: Here is an amazing example. About 95 percent of Egyptians live in the narrow Nile valley and delta. And Java, an island about the size of England, has more than 150 million people, more than the whole of Russia! Can you believe it?

explain.say: Now the almost empty places: the Sahara, Siberia, the Amazon forest, the Himalayas and Antarctica. They are too dry, too cold, too steep or too thickly forested for many people to farm and build. Which one would be hardest to live in, do you think?

explain.say: So people gather where water, flat land and good soil meet, and where there are jobs in cities. Great sorting! Challenge: look at a photo of the Earth at night from space, and find the crowded places glowing bright.

faq.a: Population density is the number of people living on each square kilometre. Among big countries, Bangladesh is one of the most crowded, with over 1,000 people per square kilometre, while Mongolia has only about 2.
asks: Which country is the most crowded?

faq.q: Why do so many people live in river valleys?
faq.a: Rivers give water for drinking and farming, flat land and fertile mud from floods, and an easy way to travel. The first great civilisations grew beside the Nile, the Indus, the Tigris and Euphrates, and the Yellow River.
asks: Why did early civilisations start by rivers?
Why do so many people live by rivers?

faq.q: Why do so few people live in deserts and mountains?
faq.a: Deserts lack water, and mountains are steep, cold and hard to farm or build roads on. Very cold places like Siberia and Antarctica have short growing seasons or none at all.
asks: Why is the Sahara almost empty?

faq.q: How many people live on Java?
faq.a: More than 150 million people live on Java, making it the most populous island on Earth, though it is only about the size of England.
asks: What is the most crowded island?

faq.a: Sparsely populated means few people spread over a large area, like the Sahara or Mongolia. Densely populated means many people living close together, like Java or Bangladesh.
asks: What is the difference between sparse and dense?

facts: Java, Indonesia, is the world's most populous island, home to more than 150 million people.
About 95% of Egypt's people live in the Nile valley and delta.
Mongolia is the most sparsely populated independent country, with about 2 people per km².
